sections.content: You know *como si* from B2 Unit 15: it compares with something unreal and takes the imperfect subjunctive (*Habla como si lo supiera todo*). You also know the pluperfect subjunctive from B2 Unit 16, which you use when the imagined thing comes before the main verb: *Habló de la selva como si la hubiera visto* ("as if he had seen it"). New here: *igual que si* and *lo mismo que si* mean "just as if" and follow the same rule. The verb after them is never in the indicative or the present subjunctive.

items.spanish: Habla como si lo supiera todo.
items.english: He talks as if he knew everything.

items.spanish: Habló de la selva como si la hubiera visto.
items.english: He spoke about the jungle as if he had seen it.

items.spanish: Me trató igual que si fuera de la familia.
items.english: She treated me just as if I were part of the family.

items.spanish: Actuó lo mismo que si no hubiera pasado nada.
items.english: He acted just as if nothing had happened.

sections.content: Compare *como quieras* (B2 Unit 32, lesson 4) with *como si quisieras*. The first is about a real choice and uses the present subjunctive. The second compares with something unreal and uses the imperfect subjunctive.
